status.en: 9 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 18% fewer than the week before, most of them in La Espriella, Cucuta and Bogota.
status.nb: 9 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 18 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i La Espriella, Cucuta og Bogota.

summary.en: Armed men seized a supermarket in Cartagena, taking at least 25 hostages and prompting armed police to surround the site. Simultaneously, a car bomb exploded in a central Colombian city, destroying buildings and injuring more than 20 people, while another car bomb hit the governor's office in Meta. The ELN carried out a drone strike on a police base, injuring three people including an infant, and a separate drone strike hit a Colombian city. The Colombian president blamed ex-FARC rebels for the car bomb blast. Violence remains high, with 225 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Væpnede menn tok kontroll over et supermarked i Cartagena, tok minst 25 gisler og førte til at bevæpnede politifolk omringet stedet. Samtidig eksploderte en bilbombe i en sentral colombiansk by, ødela bygninger og såret mer enn 20 personer, mens en annen bilbombe traff guvernørkontoret i Meta. ELN utførte et droneangrep på en politibase, såret tre personer inkludert et spedbarn, og et separat droneangrep traff en colombiansk by. Den colombianske presidenten la skylden på eks-FARC-opprørerne for bilbombeeksplosjonen. Voldnivået forblir høyt, med 225 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Colombian conflict
background.extract: The Colombian conflict began on May 27, 1964, and is a low-intensity asymmetric war between the government of Colombia, paramilitary groups, crime syndicates, and far-left guerrilla groups engaged in armed factional hostilities to increase their influence in Colombian territory. Some of the most important international contributors to the Colombian conflict include multinational corporations, the United States, Cuba, and the drug trafficking industry.
